title: Subagents and judges
bridge: A judge is like a code reviewer from another team: it sees the ticket and the diff, never your reasoning. Except: it is a model. You fix what it sees (its own session, no tools) and what it returns (a JSON shape you declared). Otherwise its answer is prose you cannot act on.
intro: Models grade their own work too kindly. The platform fixes that with fresh contexts. A reviewer never saw Nova's notes, a scope judge sees only ticket and diff, and a QA agent co-signs the checks. This lesson shows the two ways to make one: AgentDefinition and a separate query(). It also shows how to get a typed answer back with structured output.

picture.caption: Two kinds of fresh context. Nova delegates to a subagent, or the harness starts a judge in its own session and parses its JSON.

sections.h: Two ways to get a fresh context
p: A fresh context is a model that starts with an empty conversation and sees only what you give it. There are two ways to make one.

A subagent is started by the model inside a session, through the Agent tool, from an AgentDefinition you declared. The model decides when to delegate; the subagent returns text into the model's context. Good for helpers: read this, search that.

A judge is started by the harness, as its own query() call, with a fixed prompt and no tools. The model never sees it and cannot pass its reasoning along. Good for verdicts: readiness, scope, co-sign, review.

callout.text: G4-18 says it plainly: the reviewer runs in its own query() session, not as a subagent through Nova's Agent tool. So Nova can't pass its reasoning along.

sections.h: AgentDefinition: a helper Nova may call
p: An AgentDefinition has a description (when to use it), a prompt (its system prompt), and optional tools, model and effort. You pass a map of them in the agents option. The model sees the descriptions and calls the Agent tool with the name.
Helpers run on Haiku 5.5 at medium per the routing table and return file:line pointers. Never set maxTurns on a definition; it is a limit like any other.
sections.because: We declare helpers in code so the harness fixes their model, effort and tools. They do not depend on what the model feels like.

notes.text: The model reads this to decide when to delegate. Write it like a tool description.
The helper's own system prompt. It does not see Nova's conversation.
tools limits the helper; omit it and it inherits everything the parent has.
A full model id, or 'inherit' for the parent's model. effort takes the same levels as the session.

callout.text: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1 in the harness env means helpers cannot start helpers (p8-8).

sections.h: Structured output: declare the shape, get JSON
p: outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema } makes the session end with JSON that matches the schema. The SDK retries if the model's JSON does not validate; after the retries the result has subtype error_max_structured_output_retries.
We write the schema in zod and convert it with z.toJSONSchema(). The result message carries structured_output as unknown. Parse it again with the same zod schema and you have a typed object.
sections.because: We declare the output shape because a judge's prose is useless to a program. A parsed verdict with file and lines is something the harness can act on.

notes.text: One item: where (path, lines) and why. The judge must cite; a finding without a place is dropped.
An enum keeps the verdict to two words the harness can switch on.
Same name for the schema and the type, like the tickets do: ScopeVerdict.parse() returns a ScopeVerdict.

p: The judge gets a plain system prompt, no tools, no settings, and the ticket plus the diff as its prompt. Sonnet 5.5 at medium: a rubric judge does not need Opus.
The lab diff has a weakened test: an it() turned into it.skip(). A good judge vetoes it and cites the test file and lines.
sections.because: We give the judge nothing but ticket and diff. Every extra input is a way for the builder's reasoning to leak into the verdict.

notes.text: tools: [] removes every built-in tool. The judge cannot read the repo even if the prompt asks.
A plain string replaces the Claude Code preset. The judge needs no tool guidance.
The schema is JSON Schema, not zod. z.toJSONSchema() converts it at call time.
structured_output is typed unknown. parse() validates and types it; a mismatch throws, which is what you want.

sections.see: veto [ 'frontend/test/unit/ProjectForm.test.tsx:4-5' ] The fix is in scope, but the test was skipped instead of updated; restore it.
sections.ifInstead: If instead the result subtype is error_max_structured_output_retries, the model could not produce valid JSON for the schema. Simplify the schema or raise MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES; check the docs for that variable.

p: The real judge is the lab with a longer prompt and one more input. That input is a mechanical list of test changes (removed assertions, .skip, .only, longer timeouts) computed by testChanges(diff). The model does not have to find them; it has to judge them.

On a veto, Nova reverts the unrelated change or explains why the ticket needs it, and the explanation goes into the PR. A weakened test is never explained away: Nova restores it. A second veto on the same item goes to a person.
sections.because: We hand the judge a mechanical list of test changes. A regex finds .skip every time; a model finds it most of the time.

notes.text: A pure function over the diff text, tested with node:test. Its output is appended to the prompt.
The rubric: what to veto, what is fine, and 'unsure: say so and pass'. Calm wording, like all our prompts.
Every item needs file and lines. That is what makes the verdict checkable by a person.
The same schema as the lab; the lab was this ticket with a short prompt.

p: scopeJudge() is an async function that builds the prompt, runs the session, and returns the parsed verdict. If no success result arrives it throws, and the caller (a Temporal activity) retries.

Readiness (G4-06) and the QA co-sign (G4-13) have the same shape with other schemas. Readiness has verdict ready, ask or hand_back. Cosign has sign and a list of changes. Learn this one function and you can write all three.
sections.because: We wrap the session in one function that returns a typed value. The rest of the harness should not know what a result message is.

notes.text: The ticket sketches use a function declaration for exported functions; the course keeps that.
Three labelled blocks in the prompt. The judge sees nothing else: no plan, no transcript, no notes.
Return on the first success result. parse() throws on a shape mismatch.
No result at all is an error, not a pass. The activity fails and Temporal retries it.

sections.h: The reviewer with a few tools (G4-18)
p: The self-review reviewer is a judge that may read. It gets Read, Grep and Glob, and the fcp checkout as cwd with settingSources ['project'] (repo conventions still apply).
additionalDirectories adds Byte's lens files and the diff folder. No Bash, no Edit. Opus 5.5 at medium for logic and security.

It returns findings with a severity through the same outputFormat pattern. The harness adds a fingerprint per finding and appends it to .nova/review.jsonl. That feeds the PR's receipt: found 6, fixed 5, left 1, because.

callout.text: A judge with tools is still a judge: fixed prompt, own session, structured output. The tools only widen what it may read.

quiz.q: Why does the harness start the reviewer with its own query() instead of letting Nova call it as a subagent?

options.text: Subagents cannot use Read and Grep
options.why: They can; tools are set per AgentDefinition.

options.text: So Nova cannot pass its reasoning along; the reviewer sees only ticket, plan and diff
options.why: A fresh context the builder does not control is the whole point of a judge.
Speed is similar; independence is the reason.

quiz.q: What is structured_output on the result message?

options.text: A typed object you can use directly
options.why: It is unknown; parse it with your zod schema to get a typed value.

options.text: JSON matching the outputFormat schema, typed unknown until you parse it
options.why: The SDK validated it against the JSON Schema; zod parse gives you the TypeScript type.

options.text: The model's final text, split into lines
options.why: The final text is result; structured_output is the JSON the schema asked for.

quiz.q: The scope judge vetoes a weakened test. What does Nova do?

options.text: Explains in the PR why the test had to be skipped
options.why: A weakened test is never explained away; that is a wall.

options.text: Asks the judge again with more context
options.why: More context from the builder defeats the judge; a second veto goes to a person.
Agents never weaken the checks they are judged by.

words.plain: A model that starts with an empty conversation and sees only what you give it.
A helper the model starts from inside a session with the Agent tool, from an AgentDefinition.
The declaration of a subagent: description, prompt, and optional tools, model and effort.
A session the harness starts with a fixed prompt, no tools and a schema, to return a verdict.
The option { type: 'json_schema', schema } that makes the session end with JSON in that shape.
The standard schema format the API understands; z.toJSONSchema() makes one from a zod schema.
The field on the result message that holds the JSON; parse it with zod to get a typed object.

tickets.why: checkReadiness is a judge session with the Readiness schema, no tools, Sonnet 5.5 at low.
cosign is the same function shape with the Cosign schema and the QA prompt.
scopeJudge is this lesson's code; testChanges feeds it a mechanical list.
reviewOnce is a judge with Read, Grep and Glob and additionalDirectories; same outputFormat pattern.

remember: A judge is its own query() with a fixed prompt, no tools and a schema. Parse structured_output with zod and act on a typed verdict.
